ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Art. 305bis and 305ter Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) on money laundering and lack of financial due diligence; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG; SR 955.0) and AMLA-FINMA Ordinance (SR 955.01); Art. 4 AMLA economic-beneficiary definition; Art. 61 and Art. 697l Code of Obligations (SR 220) on registered office and internal share register; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV; SR 221.411) Arts. 15-18; Swiss sanctions ordinances implemented by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and the Directorate of International Law.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - no public Swiss UBO register; companies maintain a private share register (Art. 697l CO) recording holders and beneficial owners above 5% of registered shares; financial intermediaries and notaries verify economic beneficiaries under Art. 4 AMLA at a 25% threshold; data is obtainable by criminal/AML authorities (MROS, FINMA, prosecutors) but not by the public; nominee structures are possible but trigger enhanced banking KYC and can raise AML and tax red flags.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss public-notary authentication; no apostille required for domestic Swiss use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin (registry/notary) plus Swiss-certified translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country of origin is a Hague Convention member) or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified Swiss translation (German, French or Italian)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank or FINMA-regulated securities intermediary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct acknowledgement by the notary; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director and signatory against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) Swiss SECO consolidated state and asset-freeze sanctions list; (iii) OFAC SDN list and EU consolidated sanctions list as best practice given USD-denominated SaaS revenue via Stripe/Paddle; (iv) PEP registers under the FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance and the Swiss Bankers Association Due Diligence Agreement (VSB-20), with enhanced due diligence for PEPs and close associates; verification includes certified ID/address evidence, AML adverse-media checks and 10-year AMLA record retention.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Federal Commercial Register Main Register (Hauptregister / Registre principal), searchable via the Zefix Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch); preliminary name clearance filings are submitted to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name must use Latin alphabetic script (Latin-1 character set; German umlauts and French/Italian diacritics permitted). No Chinese characters or script beyond Latin is accepted in the registry; if the parent brand is in non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese), a phonetically transliterated Latin form is mandatory for registry use and must appear in the notarial deed. Informal second-line Chinese branding may be used in marketing materials but has no legal registry effect. The name must include the mandatory suffix AG or SA and must be truthful, distinctive, and not misleading (Art. 950 CO; Arts. 30-32 HRegV).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Official cantonal or municipal coat-of-arms references requiring authorisation (Art. 31 HRegV)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under Art. 16 HRegV the preliminary name clearance (Vorentscheid) remains valid for 3 months and lapses automatically if incorporation is not filed within that period; no formal extension is available, but a fresh preliminary decision may be obtained with the same or a revised name. Upon rejection the applicant may: (1) modify the offending token and resubmit; (2) request a reasoned written decision from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office within 10 working days; (3) file a supervisory complaint with the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehoerde) within 30 days; (4) appeal to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) under the Federal Administrative Procedure Act; where the objection is based on a third-party trademark, a written co-existence undertaking from the prior IP holder (verified via the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property, SwissTMsearch) should accompany the rebuttal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial - a pure virtual letterbox without business substance is insufficient. The Aktiengesellschaft must designate a verifiable Swiss registered office where central administration is in fact conducted (Art. 61 CO). For a low-risk SaaS/MarTech analytics tool, a serviced business address with physical premises, mail handling, records retention and available meeting space is accepted by Swiss registries and banks; a purely virtual mailbox domiciliation is inconsistent with FINMA, VSB-20 and substantive corporate substance expectations and materially increases Swiss bank onboarding rejection risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 8% annual probability for a standard low-risk, unlicensed MarTech SaaS; desk-based substance checks by cantonal commercial register and business audit authorities are routine on a sampled basis; unannounced physical inspection risk rises to approximately 25% only where the address appears on public letterbox or domiciliation-only lists or where AML indicators (bearer shares, nominee layers, non-resident director concentration) are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Articles 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Article 626 (minimum nominal capital); Article 632 (minimum paid-up capital); Articles 628-630 (escrow of capital contributions); Articles 640-643 (registration requirements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce), administered under the supervision of the Federal Commercial Register and published via the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (FOSC / SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde / Acte constitutif) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts) filed for entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is CHF 100,000 fully subscribed in registered bearer or registered shares; at least 20% of the nominal value per share, and in any event no less than CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash prior to registration. The paid-up funds must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto / compte de consignation) at a Swiss bank, with the bank's blockage confirmation presented to the Commercial Register; the funds are released only upon successful registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the First Meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company] AG: 1. Share Subscription. The Board acknowledges subscription of 1,000 registered shares at CHF 100 nominal value each, totalling CHF 100,000. The paid-up portion of CHF 50,000 has been deposited in a blocked escrow account and shall remain blocked until Commercial Register registration. 2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at [address], Zurich, Switzerland. 3. Officers. The Board appoints [Name] as Chair and CEO, [Name] as CFO and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each with individual signature authority. 4. Registration. The notary and any board member are authorised to file the incorporation and perform all ancillary acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat / Notariat cantonal) in the canton of the registered office (Zurich)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary to draft and certify the Errichtungsurkunde and Statuten. The notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of all founders, confirms that the articles comply with CO Articles 626-629, and authenticates the founders' signatures. The notarized deed must contain the firm name, registered office, purpose, share capital, share classes, and the first board members, and is then transmitted to the Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde)
Articles of Association (Statuten) in German or French
Valid passports or identity cards of all founders
Certified address proof for the registered office in Switzerland
Share subscription list and declaration of paid-up contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the founders identify drafting deficiencies, a corrective addendum may be executed and re-notarized; the Commercial Register allows submission of supplementary declarations within the statutory examination period without recommencing the entire procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-up Capital into Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or financial intermediary holding a banking licence (e.g. Zürcher Kantonalbank, UBS AG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital contribution account in the company's name (Freizügigkeitskonto / compte de consignation) at a Swiss bank. Deposit no less than CHF 50,000 representing the required paid-up fraction of the CHF 100,000 minimum capital. The bank will issue an irrevocable blockage confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register, attesting that the funds are at the company's disposal only upon production of the Commercial Register registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft notarized deed of incorporation or reference to the company being formed
Founders' identification documents
Swiss anti-money laundering KYC forms and declaration of beneficial ownership
Bank account opening resolution or instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates AML or source-of-funds queries, provide enhanced due diligence documentation such as bank references, audited financial statements of founders, or a detailed source-of-wealth statement; alternatively, select another licensed Swiss bank and submit a new blockage confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Commercial Register for Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zürich) via the Central Business Register Platform (ZEFIX)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application electronically through ZEFIX or in paper form at the cantonal Commercial Register Office. Attach the notarized deed, the Articles of Association, the bank's blockage confirmation, written acceptance of office by each board member and the auditor, and the signed specimen signatures. The Registrar verifies formal and substantive compliance with CO Articles 640-643 and, upon approval, issues the entry; the registration is then published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (FOSC).
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde)
Articles of Association (Statuten)
Bank blockage confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) of the escrowed paid-up capital
Written consents and declarations of the board members and statutory auditor
Passport copies and signature specimens of directors
Duly executed power of attorney if a filing agent is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues an examination query (Verfügung / réquisition), cure the identified deficiencies within the prescribed period, usually 30 days, by filing a corrective declaration or amending the deed; if the application is refused, appeal to the cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration Post-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (Steueramt des Kantons Zürich); Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC); Cantonal Social Security Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse / Caisse de compensation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register entry, the company is automatically registered with the Cantonal Tax Office for corporate income tax, wealth tax and withholding tax purposes. Separately register for VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if actual or expected annual worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; digital SaaS services are taxable at the standard rate. Register as an employer with the compensation office for AHV/AVS, ALV/AC (unemployment insurance) and EO/APG (loss of earnings) contributions, and with SUVA for mandatory occupational accident insurance, and register for institutional and individual pension schemes (BVG/LPP).
required_dossiers: Commercial Register entry extract after incorporation
Completed VAT registration form (Form 17 / Formulaire 17)
Employer registration form for the compensation office (AHV-Ausweiskarte)
Articles of Association and notarized deed
Identity documents of the persons authorised to sign
Declaration of expected turnover and payroll for provisional contribution assessments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities or compensation office require supplementary particulars, submit a written business description and projected financial statements; assessments and registrations are retroactive to the Commercial Register entry date and may be amended upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Clearance Confirmation for Digital MarTech Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO); Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM / OFCOM) for optional confirmations; Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC / EDÖB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the SEO content analytics and keyword ranking software does not constitute a telecommunications service or broadcasting activity requiring a licence under the Swiss Telecommunications Act or the Radio and Television Act. For a pure Software-as-a-Service analytics operation, no sectoral operating licence is imposed; nonetheless, document compliance with the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP / nLPD), including a register of processing activities, privacy notice, and adequacy measures for international data transfers, and obtain an optional written exemption confirmation from OFCOM if required by enterprise clients.
required_dossiers: Detailed business description and technical service specification
Data processing inventory and data flow diagram
Data protection policy and model contracts
Optional exemption request letter to OFCOM
Commercial Register extract demonstrating registered purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If OFCOM or SECO determines that the service is not covered by the ISIC 6201 software exemption and falls under a defined telecom or media activity, submit the relevant licence notification or apply for a formal classification ruling; otherwise no remedial action is necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is applicable for pure software and data analytics activities; general trade and digital economy oversight is exercised by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), with data protection supervision by the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for ISIC 6201 software publishing and SEO analytics SaaS services; no manufacturing or physical operational permit is applicable under Swiss federal or cantonal law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / OFEV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category: No EIA or preliminary environmental screening required because the activity involves no physical production facility, no construction works, and no emission-intensive installations as listed under Annex 10 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP-Verordnung / OEIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for a pure digital software operation. If the company self-hosts servers, it must comply with the Swiss Energy Act (EnG) energy efficiency requirements for data centers, the CO2 Act obligations, the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ChemRRV) for any cooling-agent handling, and the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) if cooling water discharge occurs; standard third-party cloud hosting transfers these obligations to the cloud provider.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable where the registered office is a virtual or administrative address without employees physically present. If a physical or coworking office is leased, the company must obtain fire safety certification from the Cantonal Fire Police (Kantonale Feuerpolizei), ensure compliance with structural load and earthquake safety requirements under SIA standards, and register the workplace for occupational safety inspection under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG), the Accident Insurance Act (UVG), and the EKAS operational safety directives; a workplace risk assessment and SUVA inspection clearance may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration Fédérale des Contributions AFC / Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni AFC), official portal: https://www.esty.admin.ch; Swiss central UID register portal: https://www.zefix.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Switzerland does not issue a combined national corporate TIN for all tax purposes. A Swiss AG receives a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) upon commercial register entry and obtains a cantonal taxpayer file from the competent cantonal tax authority. A foreign entity without a Swiss registered office or branch must obtain a Swiss VAT number (UID/MWST-Nr) directly from the FTA through the eService online registration portal or prescribed VAT registration form; the foreign entity must appoint a Swiss-area fiscal representative acceptable to the FTA when it has no Swiss domestic seat or establishment. A foreign AG with a Swiss permanent establishment additionally registers for Swiss federal/cantonal direct taxes via the relevant cantonal authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a separate legal person and a fully autonomous corporate income taxpayer at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. It is not transparent, pass-through, or eligible for partnership-style fiscal flow-through treatment. Non-resident AGs are subject to Swiss tax only on income attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment or on specifically Swiss-source taxable items.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss direct tax law contains no US-style check-the-box or general flow-through election for an AG. Available mechanism: (i) election for VAT group taxation (Organschaft) under the Swiss VAT Act; (ii) election for voluntary VAT registration even where the mandatory turnover threshold is not met; (iii) election to use simplified flat-rate VAT assessment (lump-sum/Saldo method) instead of actual input VAT deduction where conditions are met; (iv) transitional special statuses for qualifying holding, mixed, or principal companies under the 2020 Swiss Tax Reform, only during the applicable transition/expiry periods.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (LTVA / OBLTVA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 net turnover from supplies of goods/services the place of supply of which is in Switzerland within a business year (mandatory threshold raised from CHF 100,000 to CHF 250,000 effective 1 January 2025). A foreign supplier of digital services, including SaaS/SEO analytics, must register for Swiss VAT once this Swiss turnover threshold is exceeded, and must charge Swiss VAT at the applicable Swiss rate on taxable supplies made to Swiss recipients.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time tax-authority clearance, no national API-based e-invoicing clearance obligation, and no digital tax stamp for standard Swiss B2B/B2C invoices. Switzerland permits electronic invoicing and uses optional QR-billing and private-sector eBill channels. Swiss public-sector procurement is progressively moving toward e-invoicing, but there is no federal tax authority clearance mandate or live stamping mechanism for ordinary Swiss VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to export supplies of goods physically removed from Switzerland and to services supplied to recipients abroad where the place of use and enjoyment is not Switzerland. For digital SaaS/SEO analytics services, the supply is zero-rated when the customer is located outside Switzerland and the service is effectively consumed/used abroad; the taxpayer must establish the recipient's residence and the actual foreign place of benefit, with contemporaneous commercial documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (electronic or paper export declaration with customs office exit proof)
Commercial invoice containing export statement and supplier/receiver details
Bill of Lading, Airway Waybill, or CMR/road transport document evidencing physical export
Contract and payment evidence with the foreign purchaser (an inward remittance certificate is not a Swiss statutory requirement, but should be retained as audit evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss FTA actively audits export zero-rating claims and requires full, reliable evidence of export or foreign use. Missing or unreliable documentation triggers reassessment of VAT at the standard or reduced rate, plus default interest. Intentional or grossly negligent VAT evasion under Article 96 LTVA is punishable by fines of up to four times the evaded tax; negligence-based evasion carries fines up to twice the evaded tax. The assessment limitation period is generally five years after the end of the relevant tax year, extended to ten years where tax evasion is committed deliberately, and serious cases may be prosecuted under Swiss criminal tax law with additional clawback and publicity consequences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, headquartered in Zurich and Bern; foreign exchange and monetary policy functions consolidated solely at the federal level under the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank (National Bank Act, NBA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully convertible currency regime with no distinction between current and capital account transactions. The Swiss Franc (CHF, ISO 4217) is freely tradable, and there are no exchange control laws, prior licensing requirements, or import/export FX restrictions. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted; however, dividend distributions from a Swiss AG are subject to Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35%, which is normally reduced to 0-5% under an applicable double tax treaty (DTA), provided the recipient is a treaty-eligible corporate resident and an exemption certificate (Entlastungsverfügung) is obtained from the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA). Repatriation of capital (liquidation proceeds or repaid shareholder loans) is exempt from withholding tax. For SaaS/MarTech operations, no sector-specific currency licensing applies; cross-border subscription payments in USD, EUR, or CHF may be received freely into Swiss bank accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland abolished export proceeds surrender and compulsory conversion requirements in the 1960s; all export receipts, including SaaS subscriptions, digital tool licensing, and analytics service fees, may be retained in the original currency, converted freely, or held abroad. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. Only statistical reporting obligations may apply to the SNB for balance-of-payments purposes (direct investment declarations above CHF 10 million), which do not restrict FX flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (primary CHF multi-currency current account, plus segregated EUR/USD sub-accounts)
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account (domestic and cross-border payments, custody)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banca Stato Cantone / Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Treasury Account (canton-based relationship banking for SaaS exporters)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Pictet & Cie / Lombard Odier & Cie (private banks)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Treasury Escrow / Custody Account (only if institutional-quality treasury mandates required; minimums CHF 500k+)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High with strict constraints. FINMA-regulated Fintech companies (FinIA/FinSA and banking licence with FinTech deposit facility under Art. 1b Banking Act) may accept public deposits up to CHF 1 million without paying interest, but foreign EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) operating cross-border into Switzerland are not automatically passported; they must operate through a Swiss-regulated partner bank or obtain a FINMA licence for regulated deposit-taking activities. An offshore EMI account is viable as a cash-in/collection rail for low-risk SaaS revenue (Stripe/Paddle settlements), but it cannot serve as the primary fiduciary treasury account for capital injections or statutory distribution escrow. Optimal solution: maintain the tier-1 operational account at UBS/ZKB for statutory compliance and use a FINMA-supervised fintech (e.g., Rellevate, Yapeal, or Swissquote) for high-velocity card-settlement sweeps, with daily automatic sweeps into the tier-1 account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is increasingly accepted by UBS and PostFinance for Swiss-licensed directors, but the final decision is bank-specific. For a foreign-director AG (non-resident UBOs), most tier-1 Swiss banks require at least one in-person interview at the bank's premises (Zurich/Geneva) with the UBO or an authorized Swiss-resident director/trustee; a pure virtual-only opening for fully non-resident boards is generally rejected by UBS/ZKB unless a regulated Swiss fiduciary intermediary (e.g., a licensed trustee or FINMA-regulated asset manager) vouches for the KYC package. UBS Key4 SMB and PostFinance digital onboarding permit video identification for Swiss-resident directors, but all non-resident signatories must provide certified passport copies, apostilled certificates of incumbency, and a cleared negative-liability check. Budget for one physical visit by the CEO/UBO to Switzerland within 90 days of filing to satisfy residual interview requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with multi-tier offshore holding structure (e.g., holding company in a non-EU/US jurisdiction) and unclear source of funds for the initial share capital deposit (CHF 50,000 minimum paid-in for AG).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association (apostilled); (2) full UBO chain chart down to ultimate natural persons; (3) bank references from existing banks of UBOs (not older than 6 months); (4) source-of-wealth statement with supporting evidence (employment contract, sale & purchase agreement of prior company, audited financials, tax settlement receipts); (5) 3-year personal tax clearance certificates from residence jurisdiction; (6) certified passports of each UBO and signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SaaS revenue model relying on Stripe/Paddle with volume spikes from programmatic or affiliate-bot traffic, creating PEP/high-risk transaction flags or bank abrupt account-freeze trigger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed Master Subscription Agreement and terms of service; (2) sample invoice and payment-flow documentation; (3) PCI-DSS / SOC 2 Type II attestation certificates of the software platform; (4) data processing agreement (GDPR/CCPA) and privacy policy; (5) merchant processor verification letter from Stripe/Paddle confirming merchant ID and settlement schedule; (6) monthly revenue reconciliation reports matching Stripe/Paddle dashboards; (7) rejection of bot-traffic: analytics dashboard evidencing genuine organic keyword search traffic; (8) anti-fraud policy and chargeback ratio history (must be < 0.5%).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment patterns: incoming capital injection from parent/shareholder abroad immediately followed by large outbound licensing or remote-employee payroll payments, triggering antimoney-laundering suspicion of pass-through or trade-based laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) signed share subscription or shareholder loan agreement with declared purpose and repayment terms; (2) board resolution approving the capital injection and operational disbursement; (3) commercial contracts with downstream software resellers/licensees and remote consultants; (4) transfer pricing documentation (OECD TP file, local file, bench-marked comparables); (5) statutory audit reports (required for AG > CHF 2M revenue or > 50 employees, but recommended earlier); (6) agreed-upon-procedure report from a Swiss CPA firm confirming validity of the disbursement chain; (7) AML compliance officer appointment and internal AML policy per FINMA Circular 2023/1.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant SWIFT MT103 must be denominated in CHF (or EUR/USD and immediately converted upon receipt). Remittance Information (field 70) must specify 'Contribution in kind in accordance with AG Articles of Association Art. [X]' or 'Share capital increase per notarized deed of [date]' – accurate purpose code assignment is mandatory for SNB balance-of-payments statistics: use 'S0100' (exceptional financing) for equity injections, 'S0110' for subordinated shareholder loans, and 'S0990' for ordinary trade advances. Verification required by receiving bank: original notarized board resolution or shareholder resolution (Beschluss der Generalversammlung), certified list of shareholdings, and confirmation that paid-up capital meets the CHF 100,000 statutory minimum per AG law (Art. 621 CO, with CHF 50,000 mandatory paid-in); escrow account for pre-corporate-formation funds must be labeled 'Gründungskonto / Capital Escrow' and frozen until registration in the Swiss Commercial Register (SHAB).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For SaaS tool subscription royalties and licensing fees, primary clearing rails are (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT / SCT Instant) for EUR-denominated payments to EU beneficiaries, (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA USD/CHF/GBP and other currency cross-border trades, and (3) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF transactions, all executed through SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 pain.001 messages if API-connected. Commercial LC (documentary credits UCP600) is generally unsuitable for intangible software licensing and is discouraged; instead, for high-value AI-data licensing deals (> CHF 250k), use SWIFT MT103 with advance payment, or bank payment obligation (BPO) under URBPO 750 where the bank verifies digital performance obligations; if customer insists on LC, use a standby LC (SBLC, ISP98) as a performance guarantee, not as the settlement rail. Card-network settlements from Stripe/Paddle (Visa/MC/Amex settlement currencies USD/EUR/GBP/CHF) transit through acquiring banks to the operating account with a 2-day rolling settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (outrights) in USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, GBP/CHF – standard tenors up to 12 months, OTC with UBS/ZKB, requiring minimum CHF-equivalent exposure of CHF 250,000 and ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement documentation.
FX Swaps (Rolling Spot) – permissible for short-term liquidity smoothing between CHF, EUR, and USD without changing underlying exposure; commonly settled via CLS or bilateral with bank.

FX Options (plain vanilla calls/puts, EUR vs CHF and USD vs CHF) – available from tier-1 counterparties; premiums treated as treasury expense deductible for Swiss tax purposes if documented as hedging under the entity's confirmed treasury policy.

Cross-Currency Swaps – permitted but rarely used for a low-risk SaaS exporter; require a fully negotiated ISDA CSA and are not advisable below CHF 5 million notional; obtainable from UBS Global Markets or ZKB Structured Products.

NDFs (Non-Deliverable Forwards) – generally NOT permissible for CHF pairs (CHF is fully deliverable) and not recommended; NDFs available only for counterparty-requirement transactions in restricted currencies (e.g., INR, KRW, CNY), executed through UBS/Lombard Odier, and prohibited in the ordinary course unless the treasury policy explicitly authorises exotic restricted-currency hedging.

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and discharge of directors at Ordinary General Meeting
stage_5.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders (internal corporate body; no filing)
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end no later than 30 June
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability risk for directors; shareholders may petition court to convene AGM; no direct strike-off for this item, but persistent failure to comply may lead to Federal Council declaration of dissolution under Art. 731b CO in insolvency-like cases.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory rate 8.5% imposed on profit after tax, equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit; combined cantonal/municipal corporate income tax headline rates range from approximately 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (Geneva). The expected combined headline rate for the Zug-based AG is approximately 15%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday regime. Preferential instruments: (1) mandatory cantonal patent/IP box granting a 90% exemption on qualifying royalty income from patents and equivalent software rights, subject to the OECD nexus approach; (2) optional cantonal R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying Swiss R&D expenditure; (3) 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains from holdings of at least 10%; (4) deemed-paid foreign tax credit on qualifying foreign dividends. These measures can materially reduce the effective rate on software/IP income below the statutory headline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss combined federal/cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen'), consisting of the cantonal tax return form and the federal integration sheet for federal corporate income tax; filed electronically via the certified cantonal e-filing portal (e.g. Zug eTax, Zurich ZDA applications) or by paper where professional representation is not used.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within 60 to 90 days of the fiscal year-end or of service of the forms; the canton may grant extensions, commonly to 30 June for calendar-year companies; after reminder, the tax authority sets a binding final deadline under Art. 132 DBG and corresponding cantonal law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Identification block: UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), company name, legal form AG, registered seat, principal activity code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory identifier block aligning the return with the commercial register; contains issued share capital, statutory seat, director details and the principal activity code for ISIC 6201 (SEO data crawler and keyword analytics SaaS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Swiss UID of the AG; provide the foreign parent/beneficial owner in the shareholder register appendix; do not substitute foreign tax identification numbers in the Swiss UID field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Net profit per commercial balance sheet ('Reingewinn laut Handelsbilanz')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening entry: book net profit of the AG per the annual financial statements under Swiss commercial law; SaaS subscription revenue from Stripe/Paddle is recognised on an accrual basis in the period of service delivery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent's IFRS/US GAAP group profit is not substituted; the AG must file Swiss statutory accounts and may attach IFRS reconciliations only as supplementary information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Tax-addbacks outside the commercial accounts ('Aufrechnungen')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and hidden profit distributions: excessive management fees to the foreign parent, non-arm's length software royalties, mixed business expenses, unjustified value adjustments on the analytics platform intangibles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excess transfer prices paid to foreign associated enterprises and any gross-up of Swiss withholding tax not booked; attach a reconciliation to the transfer pricing documentation for cross-border SaaS transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of at least 10% or with a market value above CHF 1 million are exempt from federal and cantonal income tax; substance in the holding is not required for the deduction but is required for treaty protection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach shareholding certificates and the applicable foreign residence certificate where a dividend withholding tax refund is claimed in the same assessment; the 35% Swiss withholding tax on the AG's own distributions remains independently due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Patent box / licence box deduction ('Lizenzboxabzug')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 90% exemption of net qualifying royalty income from patents, copyrighted software and comparable IP, calculated by the nexus fraction of qualifying R&D performed in Switzerland; software code qualifies where it is patent-equivalent or protected under the software copyright box.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The deduction is limited to income attributable to the Swiss permanent establishment of the AG; a foreign IP owner without Swiss substance cannot claim the box and may be exposed to permanent establishment allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Loss carryforward and final taxable income ('Verlustvortrag' and 'Steuerbarer Reingewinn')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmed tax losses from the preceding seven years are offset against current-year income; after all adjustments the final taxable net profit is determined and the statutory rate applied; no minimum tax floor exists for AGs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign purchaser of the Swiss AG may not deduct losses generated before the change of control to the extent the business was restructured offshore; the cantonal tax office issues a loss confirmation certificate upon request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine ('Ordnungsbusse') of CHF 200 to CHF 5,000 per missed deadline and up to CHF 10,000 in aggravated cases; default reminder fee CHF 100 to CHF 500; late-payment interest of 4.0% to 4.5% per annum; if the return remains outstanding after reminders, the tax is assessed at the tax authority's discretion with a surcharge typically between 20% and 50%; deliberate under-declaration triggers criminal prosecution under Art. 175 DBG.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss federal withholding tax declaration of taxable distributions ('Verrechnungssteuer-Meldung') submitted electronically via the ESTV e-portal or approved tax software; covers dividends, taxable bond interest and other movable capital income subject to the 35% withholding tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The withholding tax on each distribution must be declared and paid within 30 days after the end of the quarter in which the distribution was made; the annual reconciliation return is due by 31 March of the following year with limited extension possibilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Distribution and beneficiary line: shareholder identification, amount of distribution, 35% tax, DTA relief indicator
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each dividend payment the form identifies the beneficiary, domicile and treaty country, the gross distribution, the 35% tax withheld, and the relief claimed (refund, partial refund, or advance exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent must provide a certificate of residence (Form 823 for corporations under most treaties) and evidence of beneficial ownership before the refund order is issued; residence-state taxation is irrelevant for the Swiss refund calculation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the AG fails to deduct and remit the 35% withholding tax, it is personally liable for the undeducted amount plus arrears interest of 4.0% per annum; intentional non-declaration constitutes a criminal offence under Art. 64 VStG punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and daily fines; falsification of the declaration may escalate to tax fraud proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% on any dividend, profit share, or other distribution of profits to shareholders under Art. 1 to 4 of the Swiss Federal Withholding Tax Act (VStG).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief follows the ESTV refund procedure: (1) the foreign beneficial owner submits a valid residence certificate (Form 823 for corporate shareholders under most Swiss DTAs) issued by its home tax authority; (2) the refund application must be filed with the ESTV within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became payable; (3) for parent companies with at least 10% shareholding in treaties providing a 0% rate, an advance exemption order may be requested before payment; relief is denied where the shareholder lacks economic substance under the principal purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on royalty or licence payments for IP, including software licence fees paid by the AG to non-residents; no withholding tax applies to ordinary interest on bank deposits or trade credit; the 35% withholding tax applies only to interest on publicly issued bonds, notes, and money-market instruments of Swiss issuers. Under Swiss DTA practice, royalty and interest withholding rates are typically reduced to 0% to 10% (e.g. royalties 0% under many treaties; interest 0% to 10% depending on the counterparty state and beneficial ownership), subject to the residence certificate and the absence of abuse.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is required where the worldwide group's consolidated gross revenue equals or exceeds CHF 50 million, consistent with BEPS Action 13. Switzerland imposes no statutory Local File monetary threshold; however, the AG must produce transfer pricing documentation within 60 days of a tax audit demand for all cross-border related-party transactions. In audit practice, related-party transactions below CHF 100,000 per category are treated as de minimis and may not require a full comparability study; above this level, arm's length pricing must be evidenced for software royalties, SaaS subscription fees, and intercompany service charges.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no dedicated Economic Substance Regulation regime in the manner of offshore hubs; economic substance is nevertheless enforced through: (1) the principal purpose test in all Swiss DTAs, which denies treaty benefits to letterbox companies; (2) the nexus requirement of the patent/IP box, which requires qualifying R&D activity in Switzerland; (3) the permanent establishment doctrine and anti-abuse jurisprudence, which reattribute income to the place where the real management and value-creating functions occur. A Zug-registered AG with no local employees, no office, and no autonomous board cannot claim treaty protection or the cantonal tax advantages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion through under-declared software revenue (Steuerhinterziehung, Art. 175 DBG and cantonal equivalents)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG books only a portion of Stripe/Paddle SaaS subscription revenue, uses non-transparent revenue-sharing arrangements with a related foreign entity for the SEO analytics platform, omits foreign bank or crypto-asset income, or claims unsupported loss carryforwards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payment of the evaded tax plus a surcharge of one to three times the evaded federal tax; cantonal surcharges are added; default interest accrues on the entire unpaid balance; repeated evasion leads to higher penalties and criminal conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's tax debt under Art. 754 CO and Art. 12 VStR where they caused the under-declaration; foreign directors are subject to judicial custody requests and extradition under bilateral assistance; Swiss debt enforcement may withdraw passports and impose exit restrictions under Art. 91 SchKG to secure payment of large public-law claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud with forged books or documents (Steuerbetrug, Art. 186 DBG; Art. 14/15 VStG)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulation of annual financial statements, creation of fictitious R&D expenses, simulation of a foreign licensee to divert profits offshore, falsification of invoices, or submission of forged residence certificates in order to obtain a 35% withholding tax refund.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Intentional tax fraud carries imprisonment of up to five years and a monetary fine of up to three times the evaded tax; the criminal proceeds and the software platform used in the offence are subject to confiscation under Art. 70 ff. StGB; corporate criminal liability permits fines up to CHF 5 million under Art. 102 StGB.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face pre-trial detention and automatic travel restrictions upon indictment; civil liability is unlimited for intentional wrongdoing; a criminal conviction triggers disqualification from serving as directors or auditors and may lead to deregistration of the AG; passports are withdrawn by the criminal judge where flight risk is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell or letterbox company lacking economic substance and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG's SaaS operations are in fact performed by a foreign group entity; the AG has no local employees, no business premises, no active board in Switzerland, and is used solely to access Zug's low tax rate, the patent box, and DTA benefits on cross-border dividends and royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority reallocates income to the entity performing the value-creating functions under Art. 129 DBG, denies treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, revokes patent box relief, and imposes default penalties of up to 100% of the under-assessed tax; withholding tax refunds are reclaimed with interest; the commercial register may initiate dissolution proceedings for abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director acting as a straw person is personally assessed for the unpaid tax where the corporate veil is pierced for intentional abuse; civil courts apply Art. 754 CO to attach personal assets of directors who knowingly maintained a sham structure; travel and asset restrictions are enforced through ordinary debt collection once corporate assets are insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering violations under the Swiss AML Act and Art. 305bis/305ter StGB
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SEO analytics tool processes payments that the AG accepts without verifying the commercial background of customers, without an internal AML policy, or without reporting suspicious transactions; proceeds derived from stolen data, ransomware, or sanctions circumvention are credited to the AG's bank accounts; the low-risk classification does not exempt the AG from suspicious transaction reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis StGB: imprisonment of up to three years, or up to five years where the perpetrator knows that the assets originate from a criminal organisation; Art. 305ter StGB punishes inadequate organisational measures with an additional fine; corporate fines up to CHF 5 million under Art. 102 StGB; the illicit funds are irrevocably confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors bear personal criminal liability for failing to implement and supervise AML controls; personal confiscation of benefits, pre-trial detention, and extradition to foreign authorities are available; conviction results in disqualification from board positions and in restrictive conditions on the AG's banking relationships, including potential forced account closure.
